about: ASD-STE100 (Simplified Technical English) descriptions of the static base tools, for ToolListMode static with ToolDescStyle ste (the A/B/C test of 17 Nov 2026). Short sentences, one idea each, active voice. Every hard limit of the full text is kept; the detail moves to guide_read { topic: "batch" }.

entries.session_state: Read the document. For each shown body: volume, area, faces, solids, size (mm). Also: the step count, running jobs, the output folder. In the window, next is one short line: what FreeCAD is doing now (a dialog and its buttons first, a sketch in edit and its DoF, an open task panel), then up to 3 likely next tools with why, then the workbench and the status bar text. No tool is named while a dialog is open: use dialog_answer. leftOut and warning: an installed add-on did not load (its tools are missing; the error says why). toolsChanged: the tool list changed since the client read it. launcher: true adds the launcher's state. mismatch: the document in front is not the agent's document; doc_switch to the agent's document binds both again. documents: every open document (name, label, unsaved, byAgent). orient: true gives only a short read: where, the documents, the agent's document, its bodies and the options. Changes nothing.
entries.guide_read: Read how to do a task: workflows and traps that the tool descriptions do not give. No topic: the index (guides, their sections, and the cost of each in tokens; start: the section to read first). topic: one guide, or a list of guides in one answer (next: the topics not read). section: one ## section, or a list. Read the Start here section first, then the sections it names. Changes nothing.
entries.batch: Run many calls in one request. You get a full answer for each call. A call is a step: the tool's name in tool, and its inputs beside it. Example: { "tool": "pd_pad", "sketch": "Sketch", "length": 6 }. calls: [step, step]. For one call, use run. For many calls with one short answer, use fast. The calls run one at a time, in order: a call sees what the calls before it made. each: { "x": [15, 45] } on a step runs it once for each value. "$x" in the inputs is the value, also inside a list. Each pass is one call. The first refused call stops the batch (stopOnError: false runs all). The calls before it stay, each its own undo step. The answer has done, refused (the call, its code, kind and error) and notRun, counted from 0. The note names the calls to send next. result: kept, ran_none, rolled_back or partial. A call with a wrong form is refused by itself, in its order. rollback: true undoes the whole batch when it stops. A batch cannot hold a batch. Use the answer of an earlier call of this batch with { "$from": 2, "$at": "bodies.0.name" } (call 2, counted from 0). Every batch writes a record in batches/ in the session folder: if an answer is lost, read the newest record before you run calls again. More fields (path, start, writeTo, lines, build, check, budget, title) and record_read: guide_read { topic: "batch" }.
entries.tool_find: Find tools. words: what the tool does, in plain words ("fillet edge"). queries: a list of searches (up to 6) and tool names (up to 20) in one call. Each hit: name, group, one line. card: a name or a list of names: get the full description and inputs (cards). Each card has two example calls. plain has every input, and a null where you give the value. ready is the same call filled from the open document, and a null where it could not fill. Copy one, and give the values named in fill. A name with a prefix, other letter case or a letter wrong is read as the name. card and queries can be in one call. groups: true lists the tool groups. group: search in one group only. Any tool can be called by name, listed or not. Where the client sends only listed tools, use run for one call. Use batch for several calls. Use fast for several calls with one short answer. Changes nothing.
entries.fast: Run many calls in one request. You get one short answer. For one call, use run. For a full answer for each call, use batch. A call is a step, the same as in batch: the tool's name in tool, and its inputs beside it. Example: { "tool": "pd_pad", "sketch": "Sketch", "length": 6 }. calls: [step, step]. each: { "x": [15, 45] } on a step runs it once for each value; "$x" in the inputs is the value. { "$from": 2, "$at": "height" } takes a value from the answer of call 2 of this block (counted from 0). Each call has the checks, approvals and undo step of its tool. A step that would be refused is found before step 1, and nothing runs. At a refusal the calls before it stay. rollback: true undoes the block. check: true only checks. The answer is one line: calls, time, objects made, volume change and health. A read is the tool get. Left-out body or sketch fields come from the session, and filled says so. guide_read { topic: "batch" } has the rules.
entries.run: Run one call. You get its full answer. The input is one step: the tool's name in tool, and its inputs beside it. Example: { "tool": "pd_pad", "sketch": "Sketch", "length": 6 }. The answer is the answer of a direct call of that tool. each: { "x": [15, 45] } runs it once for each value; "$x" in the inputs is the value. approve_file and approve_code are not run this way: call them by their own names. For many calls, use batch (a full answer for each call) or fast (one short answer).
